gatorconnect.description: Academic Allies is a student-led organization dedicated to providing academic and social support to underserved middle and high school students attending alternative schools. The organization works with students who are preparing to transition back into traditional public school settings, with the goal of helping them feel more confident and supported both academically and personally. Academic Allies volunteers provide individualized and small-group tutoring, primarily in reading and math, while also serving as mentors and positive role models. Through consistent tutoring, encouragement, motivational conversations, and mentorship, the organization aims to help students strengthen their academic skills, build confidence and resilience, and recognize their potential for future success. Academic Allies also seeks to promote educational equity by connecting university student volunteers with students who may benefit from additional academic resources and positive social support.
gatorconnect.summary: Academic Allies supports underserved middle and high school students at alternative schools through tutoring, mentorship, and encouragement. We help students build academic skills, confidence, and motivation as they prepare to return to public school.

gatorconnect.description: The University of Florida Academy of Managed Care Pharmacy (AMCP) Gainesville Student Chapter is dedicated to preparing the next generation of pharmacists to lead in managed care, industry, health systems, and other innovative practice settings. Through professional development, leadership opportunities, educational programming, networking events, and collaboration with healthcare and pharmaceutical industry leaders, our chapter equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the evolving healthcare landscape. Our organization fosters innovation, advocacy, and lifelong learning while promoting evidence-based decision-making, patient-centered care, and the principles of value-driven healthcare. Members have opportunities to participate in national competitions, research initiatives, employer networking, legislative advocacy, mentorship programs, and community outreach that strengthen both their professional growth and leadership development. As one of the largest and most active professional pharmacy organizations, the UF AMCP Gainesville Student Chapter is committed to empowering future pharmacists to improve patient access to high-quality, affordable medications while advancing the future of managed care pharmacy.
gatorconnect.summary: The UF Academy of Managed Care Pharmacy (AMCP) Gainesville Student Chapter empowers future pharmacists through leadership, professional development, industry engagement, and advocacy while advancing innovation in managed care.

gatorconnect.description: Accent A Cappella was founded in 2001 by Laura Silva and Cara Christeson, becoming the first a cappella group at the University of Florida and one of the first in the South. Over two decades later, we stand as a group run by University of Florida students of various majors, identities, voice parts, and musical interests. A principal aspect of our group’s mission statement is that we strive to create a second home for everyone involved. With this group being a long withstanding part of UF’s history and culture, it is important to recognize the message we send to our members, supporters, audience and prospective members. We value the progress of what the group has become, and want to continue to share our love of music with the world and honor the music we have made over the 25 years as a competitive a cappella group.
gatorconnect.summary: Accent A Cappella is an award-winning co-ed competitive a cappella group that was founded in 2001 at the University of Florida, formerly known as No Southern Accent.

gatorconnect.description: ACS Cancer Action Network is a University of Florida student organization dedicated to advocating for high-quality, affordable healthcare and stronger federal and state investment in cancer research funding. As a chapter aligned with the American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network (ACS CAN), the nation's leading cancer advocacy organization, we connect UF students with opportunities to make a tangible impact in the fight against cancer through grassroots advocacy, education, and community engagement. Our chapter hosts a range of programming throughout the academic year, including Advocacy and Campaign Trainings that teach members how to navigate the legislative process, contact elected officials, and support ongoing cancer policy campaigns; Guest Speaker Events featuring cancer survivors, medical professionals, and ACS CAN legislative ambassadors who share firsthand insight into the fight against cancer; and our signature Cancer Survivors' Day Lights of Hope Display, an on-campus display honoring those who have lost their battle with cancer and celebrating survivors. Membership is open to all enrolled UF students, regardless of major or prior advocacy experience. Whether you're pre-med, pre-law, interested in public health policy, or simply passionate about making a difference for cancer patients and their families, ACS Cancer Action Network offers a welcoming space to build advocacy skills, connect with like-minded peers, and contribute to a cause with real, lasting impact — both on campus and at the state and federal level.
gatorconnect.summary: ACS Cancer Action Network is a UF student chapter advocating for affordable, high-quality healthcare and stronger cancer research funding through advocacy trainings, guest speaker events, and the Lights of Hope display honoring those affected by cancer.

gatorconnect.description: We are AeroGator—a student-led aerospace design team at the University of Florida. For several years, AeroGator has attracted passionate engineering students interested in the aerospace field. Our previous work includes passion projects ranging from building our own aircraft to hosting our very own UAV competitions. Our goal is to equip our students with the skills to succeed in the industry through applied engineering and skill development. In 2025, AeroGator shifted its structure to support a broader range of aerospace-related projects across UF. From designing UAVs to CAD modeling prototypes to doing competition-focused simulation work, we have established ourselves as trusted collaborators within the University of Florida engineering community. Our members work across disciplines to deliver reliable, high-quality engineering solutions while gaining hands-on experience that mirrors real-world aerospace development. We have also established professional development programs such as speaker events and workshops. Previous speakers include professionals from NASA, Collins Aerospace, and Raytheon, allowing interested members to have an insider view of the field. We have also hosted workshops in industry-relevant skills such as ANSYS, Fusion360, MATLAB, and more.

gatorconnect.description: The AI in Healthcare Club brings together pre-health students and engineering students to explore how artificial intelligence is transforming medicine. We believe the best innovations happen at the intersection of clinical insight and technical expertise, which is why our club unites students headed into healthcare careers with those building the technology that will shape it. Together, we study real-world applications of AI in medicine, from improving patient outcomes to reducing physician burnout and addressing persistent challenges in the healthcare system. Our mission is threefold: to learn collaboratively across disciplines, to build a strong professional network, and to stay focused on using technology to genuinely improve community health. Whether you're pre-med, pre-nursing, studying biomedical engineering, or just curious about where AI and healthcare intersect, there's a place for you here!
gatorconnect.summary: AI in Healthcare Club unites pre-health and engineering students to explore AI's role in medicine in improving care, reducing burnout, and tackling healthcare's toughest challenges. Join us to learn together, grow our network, and drive real impact.

gatorconnect.description: The AI² Center Student Club serves as the liaison between UF's Artificial Intelligence Academic Initiative Center and the student body. UF has built AI into the curriculum across every college, and our job is to make that accessible to students no matter what they study. Whether you're in nursing, journalism, business, or computer science, AI is already changing your field, and you should be part of shaping how. What We Do Our club programming runs through six student-led committees: Teaching & Learning: Workshops across majors, AI office hours, and peer mentorship for every student. Connections: Socials and partnerships that link students across majors and communities. Future of Work: Industry speakers and career panels about what AI means for the job you're heading toward. Research: Building essential research skills and helping you find lab and project opportunities across campus. Technological Advancements: Technical workshops and student-led projects where you build with AI. Law and Policy: Faculty panels and regular reports about the ethics and regulation of AI. Alongside committee events, we host monthly general body meetings and collaboration events with other student organizations. Who Should Join Everyone. Our members range from students who have never written a line of code to graduate researchers publishing in the field. If you're curious about AI, or skeptical of it, there's a place for you here. Get Involved Join our Discord Check out our events Follow us on Instagram: @aiclub_uf Questions: aiclub@ufsa.ufl.edu Want to lead? Committee positions open up at the beginning of each semester. Join the Discord and reach out to any officer.
gatorconnect.summary: The AI² Center Student Club serves as the official liaison between the AI² Center and the student body. Our goal is to build an AI-literate community across all majors through workshops, speaker events, and hands-on projects open to every skill level.

gatorconnect.description: Alpha Epsilon Delta (AED) – Florida Alpha Chapter is the #1 ranked Alpha Epsilon Delta chapter in the nation and the largest collegiate pre-health organization at the University of Florida. As the nation's premier pre-health honor society, our mission is to support students pursuing careers in healthcare by providing meaningful opportunities for service, professional development, leadership, research, and mentorship. Each semester, AED offers over 400 service hour opportunities through partnerships with organizations such as Florida Diabetes Camp, Climb for Cancer Foundation, UF Health, Keira Grace Foundation, and many other local and national nonprofit organizations. In addition, our chapter raises over $30,000 each semester in support of our philanthropies, allowing members to make a meaningful impact both on campus and throughout the community while strengthening their preparation for professional school. AED provides members with valuable professional resources, including physician and healthcare panels, admissions and standardized test workshops, research opportunities, shadowing connections, clinical experiences, peer mentorship, networking with healthcare professionals, and guidance throughout the medical, dental, PA, pharmacy, nursing, and other pre-health application processes. To help new members transition into college and make the most of their AED experience, we also offer a Big/Little Mentorship Program, which pairs newer members with experienced upperclassmen for guidance, support, and lasting friendships. Beyond academics and service, AED fosters a welcoming and supportive community where members build lasting friendships through socials, intramural sports, philanthropy events, volunteer activities, networking opportunities, and our Big/Little program. Our goal is to help students grow both personally and professionally while preparing them for successful careers in healthcare. Founded nationally in 1926, Alpha Epsilon Delta has grown to more than 180 chapters and over 144,000 lifetime members, making it the world's largest honor society dedicated exclusively to pre-health students. The Florida Alpha Chapter at the University of Florida, established on May 3, 1930, has earned national recognition through its commitment to excellence in service, leadership, scholarship, and member development. We welcome students from all pre-health pathways and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where individuals of every background can thrive. Interested in joining AED? Recruitment takes place during the first two weeks of both the fall and spring semesters, with applications typically closing at the end of the recruitment period. To learn more, complete our interest form, visit our website, and follow us on Instagram @UFAED for updates on recruitment, events, and opportunities. Interest Form: https://forms.gle/Azb5x1LZta7CbYjDA
gatorconnect.summary: UF's Alpha Epsilon Delta is the nation's #1 ranked chapter, offering 400+ service opportunities and raising $30,000+ each semester while connecting pre-health students with mentorship, leadership, research, and professional growth.

gatorconnect.description: Black Men in Medicine is a pre-health organization committed to advancing, supporting, and empowering Black men pursuing careers across the healthcare professions. The organization centers the experiences of Black and African American men while recognizing the complex position they occupy within educational institutions, healthcare systems, and society more broadly. Through its foundational principles of Knowledge, Service, and Mentorship , Black Men in Medicine provides members with opportunities for academic development, professional preparation, community engagement, networking, and meaningful mentorship. The organization also educates members about the structure of the current healthcare system, the historical and present-day factors that shape health outcomes, and the social, economic, and institutional barriers that affect both healthcare professionals and the communities they serve. Beyond career preparation, Black Men in Medicine creates space for thoughtful discussion about masculinity, identity, leadership, representation, and the experiences of boys and men in the United States and throughout the African diaspora. By connecting healthcare education with cultural awareness, service, and advocacy, the organization prepares members not only to enter healthcare professions, but also to become informed leaders capable of improving the systems and communities around them.

As a tri-campus organization, BSPhA connects students across the University of Florida College of Pharmacy's Gainesville, Jacksonville, and Orlando campuses, creating a lasting network of support, leadership, friendship, and professional growth.

gatorconnect.description: Bridge to SOAR is a student-led organization dedicated to promoting mental health, emotional well-being, and positive youth development through educational outreach and community engagement. The organization seeks to provide children with practical, age-appropriate lessons that introduce foundational concepts related to emotional awareness, resilience, self-confidence, healthy coping strategies, communication, stress management, and overall well-being. Through structured activities, interactive lessons, mentorship, and service initiatives, Bridge to SOAR aims to make conversations surrounding mental health more accessible, positive, and developmentally appropriate for younger populations. The organization emphasizes early education and prevention by helping children develop the skills necessary to recognize and express emotions, navigate challenges, build healthy relationships, and seek support when needed. In addition to serving children in the surrounding community, Bridge to SOAR provides university students with meaningful opportunities to participate in service, mentorship, leadership, educational programming, and community outreach. Members may contribute to the development of lesson materials, facilitate activities, support outreach efforts, collaborate with community partners, and help organize events focused on youth wellness and mental health education. Bridge to SOAR is committed to creating a supportive, inclusive, and responsible environment in which both student members and the children they serve can grow. By connecting university students with younger members of the community, the organization hopes to strengthen awareness of mental and emotional well-being while fostering empathy, resilience, confidence, and healthy habits from an early age. Ultimately, Bridge to SOAR seeks to help build a stronger foundation for lifelong well-being by equipping children with practical tools for understanding themselves, responding to challenges, and maintaining healthy emotional and social development. Through education, mentorship, and sustained community engagement, the organization strives to empower young people to develop the confidence and skills necessary to thrive.

Throughout the semester, we plan to host ADHD-friendly study sessions, engaging social opportunities, and interactive workshops surrounding topics such as career development, social skills, and mental wellness. Whether you've been diagnosed with ADHD, believe you may be neurodivergent, or even hope to learn more and support others, this organization welcomes you.

gatorconnect.description: The buildOn Club at the University of Florida is a student-led organization dedicated to breaking the cycle of poverty through education, service, and leadership. The club connects UF students with buildOn’s global mission of expanding access to education while creating meaningful opportunities to serve locally and internationally. The club will educate students about global education inequality and the barriers communities face in accessing quality education. Members will participate in fundraising campaigns, service initiatives, awareness events, and community-building efforts that directly support buildOn’s programs around the world. The club will also provide students with opportunities to participate in buildOn Treks, where volunteers work alongside local communities to construct schools and support educational development. Beyond fundraising and service, the organization aims to develop students as engaged and socially responsible leaders. Members will gain experience in leadership, event planning, fundraising, collaboration, and community outreach while working toward a shared global purpose. Ultimately, buildOn at UF seeks to turn awareness into action. By bringing together students who believe in the power of education and service, the club will create a community committed to making a lasting impact both at the University of Florida and around the world.
gatorconnect.summary: The buildOn Club at UF empowers students to fight poverty through education and service by fundraising, raising awareness, serving local communities, and supporting school construction projects worldwide.

gatorconnect.description: Student-led initiative where we custom-design LEGO models of healthcare environments. Growing up, LEGOs were a way for many of us to make sense of the world. They helped turn everyday life into something we could imagine and control. This same belief is what inspired the creation of Built 4 Joy. We want to make clinical spaces more approachable for children. By bringing the healthcare environment to an interactive scale, we aim to build familiarity, reduce anxiety, and create opportunities for children to explore on their own terms. Hands-on play allows kids to learn and explore simultaneously, while giving them control. We partner with local hospitals, clinics, organizations, and professionals to design, volunteer, and donate these packages to pediatric patients. Current sets include a surgical room, dental clinic, PT gym, and a radiology set. We are currently in the process of designing more sets and medical tools, including oncology, ophthalmology, allergy, and pediatric clinics. We use software to design LEGO models, and then buy the bricks with our funds. Then, we partner with clinics and hospitals to donate the packages to them, so they can implement them into their healthcare. We offer our members opportunities to work in design, volunteering, outreach, communications, and finance. This offers students a space to be themselves and get involved in an initiative that aligns with their hobbies, interests, and goals by making their experiences unique and fun. Everything we make is created with love and meant to bring joy into the world.
gatorconnect.summary: We design and donate LEGO models of healthcare environments for pediatric patients. Our goal is to make clinical spaces more approachable for children by reducing anxiety and building familiarity through an interactive experience.

Beyond that, we help members prepare for technical interviews and C++ roles, and we aim to put students face-to-face with C++ professionals from those industries. gatorconnect.description: At UF’s Circle K International, or CKI, chapter, we bridge the gap between campus life and the surrounding Gainesville community by devoting ourselves to improving the lives of others and creating sustainable change. Our mission is centered on three core tenets: Service, Fellowship, and Leadership. Service: In UF CKI, there are multidinous opportunities to take hands-on action in the community, with several volunteering events every week. UF CKI members collaborate with local youth, fellow students, and community partners to address diverse societal needs. Globally and locally, our service efforts target four critical initiatives: mental health, environmental justice, food & housing insecurity, and childhood development. Our widespread efforts create an opportunity for everyone to get involved and make a meaningful difference. Fellowship: Beyond service, CKI is a welcoming and kind community, where you are sure to belong. We emphasize inclusivity and connection through an active social calendar. With multiple social events every month, it is easy to transform from service event acquaintances to lifelong friends. Just one other example is our Big-Little program, our cornerstone mentorship initiative designed to welcome new members and build lasting bonds. We also promote inclusivity by providing carpooling for every single off-campus event, taking time for icebreakers at weekly meetings, and having no active membership requirement to attend any of our events! Leadership: UF CKI offers unparalleled professional and personal growth opportunities to help every member find their voice, creating leaders that will continue to foster positive change. We offer a diverse range of leadership roles, including 5 executive board positions and over 15 specialized committee chair positions that span service, socials, Kiwanis family relations, recruitment, philanthropy, scrapbooking and more! We offer several positions that start in the spring semester for incoming freshman to get an early start in leadership as well. CKI also provides a hands-on shadowing program, allowing members to gain organizational experience and the opportunity to help plan their own official event. CKI leaders exude servant leadership, with a cohesive team dedicated to supporting, elevating, and building up each and every member. Our Pledge: I pledge to uphold the object of Circle K International, to foster compassion and goodwill towards others through service and leadership, to develop my abilities and the abilities of all people, and to dedicate myself to the realization of humanity's potential. Motto: Live to Serve, Love to Serve. Core Tenets: Service Fellowship Leadership
gatorconnect.summary: CKI empowers students to become compassionate leaders through impactful community service and lifelong fellowship. As part of the world’s largest student-led service organization, we are dedicated to fostering positive change in Gainesville and beyond.

Establishing annual cultural activities on campus to educate the student body about Haiti. Assisting members of the student body interested in learning about Haitian culture. Recruiting Haitian and other students of the University of Florida. Supporting the effort of achieving diversity on campus. To ensure that the organization attains its goals, the following activities shall be the responsibilities of the Executive Board: Organizing professional workshops and seminars Hosting social events Recruiting new members Promoting Haitian culture Making a positive impact on the community Representing the organization with integrity. Club Creole maintains a stance of political neutrality. This means the organization upholds the principle of impartiality, avoiding partisan bias in political matters, situations, or roles. Club Creole does not support any side in disagreements, conflicts, or elections and remains unbiased and objective. This ensures the organization maintains trust, credibility, and impartiality. Individual members may express personal opinions. However, Club Creole as an organization will not take positions on policies, major political issues, or elections. Members may speak as individuals, but the organization itself will not be publicly associated with any political party, candidate, or political organization. This policy reinforces the independence and neutrality of Club Creole in all public and campus-related matters.

gatorconnect.description: Dance Marathon at the University of Florida is a yearlong philanthropic effort benefiting the patients of UF Health Shands Children's Hospital in Gainesville, Florida. Each year, students stay awake and on their feet at our annual 26.2 hour event to raise funds and awareness for Children's Miracle Network for the duration of the event. In the 32 years of Dance Marathon at UF's existence, we have raised more than $34 million , making it the most successful student-run philanthropy in the Southeastern United States . In 2026, DM at UF raised a grand total of $1,152,326.32 for UF Health Shands Children's Hospital, our local Children’s Miracle Network hospital. In 2023, UF Health Shands Children's Hospital treated children from 66 counties in Florida, 49 other states, and 7 other countries. There were 18,586 telehealth visits, 40,408 ER visits, and 359,419 clinic visits. All of the funds raised by DM at UF go directly to purchasing state-of-the-art medical equipment, enhancements to make the children’s stay at the hospital more enjoyable, and funding for research grants and educational programs . Patient care funding provides necessities such as bandages and patient gowns, as well as equipment and hospital improvements to make hospital stays more enjoyable for children and their families. Research funding helps our doctors find solutions for incurable diseases such as cystic fibrosis and cancer, and it allows them to develop life-saving technology and enhanced processes that improve the daily lives of pediatric patients. Education funding supports programs such as Child Life Diversion therapy and goes toward raising funds and awareness for the Children’s Miracle Network. As we head into our 33rd year, Dance Marathon at UF is excited to make even more miracles!
gatorconnect.summary: Dance Marathon at the University of Florida is the largest student-run and highest fundraising philanthropy on campus. Our mission is to bring together campus and community to raise funds and awareness for our local UF Health Shands Children Hospital.

gatorconnect.description: DSSD’s mission is twofold: first, to give students at UF (from all majors and skill levels) hands-on data science learning and professional development opportunities through real-world projects, and second, to provide consistent technical support to partner organizations from students eager to contribute their skills. While technology is becoming increasingly essential to the successful operations of any organization, there is a shortage of technical skills to match such high demand. Many organizations are left without the expensive technical capacity required to be effective. DSSD’s goal is to bridge that technical gap by providing long-term and ongoing technical support to organizations from a team of passionate, driven students. DSSD strongly values centering the perspectives and needs of partner organizations and providing consistent support. Students from all backgrounds and skill levels will be able to join DSSD, and they can choose how they want to contribute to a project and how much time they want to commit. DSSD is dedicated to being an inclusive and supportive environment where students can work on engaging projects at the intersection of sustainable development, data, and technology. DSSD’s activities each semester will center around projects with partner organizations that may involve coding, business consultation, communication, design, writing, research, and more. DSSD will be a space where students can learn new skills and exercise the skills they learned in class by working on interdisciplinary projects that will directly benefit a partner organization. Members of DSSD will gain professional development and skill-building opportunities, as well as experience working on tangible projects to support a social-impact organization.

gatorconnect.description: Diversified Invested Student Securities (DISS) Capital is a student-run investment fund operating with a $1,000,000 virtual capital base in a sector-neutral portfolio that is benchmarked against the S&P 500 index. Our mission is to cultivate the next generation of investment professionals by providing hands-on experience in the financial markets. At the heart of our investment philosophy lies a dual approach of long and short positions, enabling us to navigate through diverse market conditions with agility and insight. Our strategy is built on rigorous analysis, leveraging both fundamental and technical research to uncover undervalued assets and identify overvalued opportunities for shorting. We believe in a disciplined investment process, focusing on long-term value creation to outperform our benchmark. Our fund is powered by a dedicated team of Investment Analysts, Associates, Sectors Leaders, and Portfolio Managers, each acting as a filter between converting investment ideas to trades. Beyond aiming for financial performance, DISS serves as a platform for real-world education in investment management. We bridge theory with practice, preparing new members as ‘Fundamental Analysts’ through a rigorous 10-week investing curriculum taught by the Portfolio Managers. Members who demonstrate an innate work-ethic and desire to learn get promoted to be an Investment Analyst in the Investment Fund. Through our program, students acquire the skills and knowledge necessary to succeed in the recruiting process and beyond. Many of our members have gone on to secure competitive internships and full-time roles at leading investment banks, private equity firms, and other top financial institutions. These opportunities not only provide valuable practical experience but also allow our members to access financial resources that can support their career development and future success in the finance industry.
gatorconnect.summary: A student-run investment fund operating with a virtual capital base in a sector-neutral equity portfolio which serves to cultivate the next generation of investment professionals through hands-on experience and career recruitment resources.

gatorconnect.description: The Environmental Law and Land Use Pre-Law Society is for students interested in careers in environmental and land use law, the fields that determine how air, water, wildlife, and public lands are protected, and how communities are zoned, planned, and built. Members meet practicing attorneys, planners, and policy staff, work through real cases, and network with nonprofits and policy organizations doing this work. We follow current events in the field, from major court decisions to permitting fights and development disputes, and build a working knowledge of the environmental and land use laws that shape Florida and Gainesville specifically: wetlands protection, water management districts, comprehensive plans, and local zoning. gatorconnect.description: The First Generation Leadership Program (FGLP) is a year-long leadership development and college transition program for first-year, first-generation students at the University of Florida. Through our pillars of mentorship, professionalism, community service, and family, FGLP empowers students to thrive both on campus and beyond. Mentorship: Via a personalized mentor-matching process, each cohort member is paired with a mentor who can offer guidance, advice, and support throughout their college journey. These connections help students feel more confident as they navigate their first year while building relationships that often continue long after the program ends. Professionalism: FGLP helps students grow both personally and professionally through workshops, networking opportunities, and hands-on experiences. Along the way, cohort members build skills in communication, leadership, networking, and teamwork that can support them both during and post-college. Community Service: As first-generation college students, we believe it's important to give back to the communities that have supported us along the way. Through service opportunities at UF, across Gainesville, and surrounding communities, cohort members make a positive impact while learning more about the people they serve. Family: At FGLP, the connections are more than networking. We build a close-knit community where students can grow together, support one another, and form lasting friendships. We understand that college comes with its challenges, so we strive to make sure every cohort member has people they can turn to for advice, encouragement, and support. Through our four pillars, FGLP creates a space where first-generation students can connect, grow, and support one another during their UF journey. These pillars shape what FGLP is all about: Being First, Together!
gatorconnect.summary: The First Generation Leadership Program (FGLP) is a year-long program that helps first-year, first-generation UF students transition to college through mentorship, professional development, service, and family.

gatorconnect.description: Florida Club Rowing was founded in 1984 as a club sport, but we have never let the classification "club" define our performance or results. We compete against program teams as well as other club teams in one of the most physically and mentally rigorous sports in the world. We practice 6 days a week on Newnans Lake in Gainesville, FL. Our season is all year round, with Head races in the Fall (5,000 meter, timed races) and sprints (2,000 meters) in the Spring. Our team started off as just a small group of passionate athletes. They rowed in mixed men/women line ups until they had enough rowers to separate into women's and men's team. Now we have grown to four full teams: Novice Women, Novice Men, Varsity Women and Varsity Men. We have pushed ourselves onto the national spotlight and are a force to be reckoned with in the rowing world. Each year we seek to expand our fleet, improve our facilities, strengthen our bodies, and perfect our stroke. With the help of dedicated athletes and encouraging coaches, family, alumni, and fans, we can achieve all of our goals and spread the Gator Nation domination throughout the rowing world.
gatorconnect.summary: Founded in 1984, Florida Club Rowing competes year-round against top collegiate and club teams. With four competitive squads, six days of training each week, and a tradition of excellence, we proudly represent Gator Nation on the national stage.

gatorconnect.description: Florida Running Club is a recreational and competitive running club at the University of Florida exclusively for UF students. We were founded in 2011, now with 135 active members all striving towards wellness and running goals. Where/When do we run? Our members participate in optional easy runs offered daily M-F at the Pearcy Beard Track at James G. Pressley Stadium at 6:30 pm. Our routes explore a different part of campus and greater Gainesville every day, typically from 2-6 miles with runners pacing anywhere from 6 min/mile to 11 min/mile. We also offer long runs on either Saturdays & Sundays at 7:00 am! Who runs with us? gatorconnect.description: The purpose of Flourish on Fifth (FOF) is to cultivate a vibrant, community-driven urban agricultural space that actively combats food insecurity, alleviates health disparities, and fosters social cohesion within Gainesville’ historic neighborhoods. Rooted in the foundational success of the Fifth Avenue Community Garden project, this organization utilizes a systems-thinking approach to promote local sustainability, food sovereignty, and neighborhood well-being. Through hands-on learning, collaborative agricultural workshops, and peer mentorship, FOF aims to replace social isolation with mutual trust and support. By empowering students and residents to manage shared green spaces, Flourish on Fifth serves as a replicable model for community resilience, long-term health equity, and environmental stewardship. The mission of the Flourish on Fifth is to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all within the historic Fifth Avenue and Pleasant Street neighborhood. Utilizing a systems thinking approach, we confront the interconnected challenges of food insecurity, limited access to mental health resources, and weakened social cohesion by examining how these structural issues interact rather than treating them in isolation. We establish inclusive, hands-on learning spaces that bridge persistent educational disparities, food insecurity, and limited access to mental health resources on Gainesville's east side. Through strategic collaboration between a dedicated student cohort, neighborhood residents, city contacts, and local historical associations, we cultivate seasonal crops, deliver interactive nutrition education, and distribute fresh produce. Our organization empowers community members to actively collaborate in creating sustainable, neighborhood-based solutions that address the root causes of well-being challenges and build long-term local resilience. Flourish on Fifth’s vision is to cultivate a thriving, self-sustaining community where every single member feels deeply nourished, socially connected, and fully empowered to contribute to collective well-being. We envision a future where the historical boundaries of the Fifth Avenue neighborhood are defined not by resource gaps or educational disparities, but by robust systems of mutual aid, localized food sovereignty, and structural resilience. By transforming shared urban spaces into dynamic centers of leadership development, ecological stewardship, and hands-on education, we strive to establish a neighborhood ecosystem that inherently fosters trust and emotional resilience across generations. Ultimately, we look forward to a long-term model of shared ownership where students, city stakeholders, and residents seamlessly co-manage a resilient, self-perpetuating network of well-being and community health.
gatorconnect.summary: The purpose of Flourish on Fifth (FOF) is to cultivate a vibrant, community-driven urban agricultural space that actively combats food insecurity, alleviates health disparities, and fosters social cohesion within Gainesville’ historic neighborhoods.

gatorconnect.description: The Gator Interior Design Club is a dynamic hub for aspiring interior designers. Our primary mission is to engage, connect, and build a cohesive community for students within our CIDA-accredited undergraduate program, while creating meaningful pathways into the professional industry. At the center of our organization is our flagship Mentor/Mentee Program, which thoughtfully pairs upperclassmen with underclassmen. This initiative provides tailored guidance to help incoming members navigate the academic rigor of the program, transition seamlessly into their professional journeys, and connect with peers for constructive feedback as they prepare for the selective admissions checkpoint after sophomore year. Complementing this peer network, we regularly host guest lectures and panels featuring alumni and industry professionals. Sessions like those offer members firsthand insight into real-world practice, industry trends, and career strategies. To cultivate well-rounded designers, we balance our calendar with both social gatherings and career-focused events. We prioritize inclusive participation across all studio levels, ensuring that every student's voice is represented as we prepare our members for excellence in the field of interior design.
gatorconnect.summary: The Gator Interior Design Club at UF builds a supportive community for interior design students through social and professional networking events, ensuring equal representation across all years within a CIDA-accredited undergraduate curriculum.

gatorconnect.description: Gator Judo Club is a student-run group of athletes and hobbyists at the University of Florida connected by our common love of judo. On the mat, the only distinction between judoka is the belt around your waist. A judoka's beliefs and background aren't an obstacle to their success. We are united by our respect for the sport and for each other. Our mission is to educate, inspire, and connect judoka throughout Florida and beyond. One of our utmost goals is to educate interested students about the values and skills we train by. Judo is a sport that requires self-discipline, mental toughness, courage, and respect. The foundation of judo involves the idea that, through training, anyone can become a skilled judoka. For this reason, we encourage our members to train hard and compete in the numerous tournaments and scrimmages we organize and attend throughout the United States. Our connections with other clubs and schools are what make these events possible, and are a key element in the judo network that we wish to build.
gatorconnect.summary: Gator Judo Club is a group of athletes and hobbyists at the University of Florida connected by our common love of judo. We hold weekly practices to teach students the principles of judo and prepare students for local scrimmages and competitions!

gatorconnect.description: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) Gator Law Chapter provides a forum for students interested in first amendment, equal protection, due process, and privacy rights, and all other civil liberties. This chapter advocates for legal protections for traditionally marginalized and vulnerable groups including women, people of color, members of the LGBTQ community, people with disabilities, and the poor. This chapter serves as an informational resource, providing details on civil liberty events around campus and in Gainesville. Our mission is to connect members with local, state and national ACLU chapters to assist their efforts and gain pro bono and internship experience. This chapter seeks to aid the ACLU national network in defending and preserving the fundamental rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States.
gatorconnect.summary: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) Gator Law Chapter provides a forum for students interested in first amendment, equal protection, due process, and privacy rights, and all other civil liberties.

gatorconnect.description: Gator Microbiome is a student organization dedicated to educating students of all backgrounds about the human microbiome and its powerful connections to nutrition, health, and everyday life. We make microbiome science accessible and engaging so that students do not need a background in science or healthcare to participate. Through educational events and interactive activities, members can explore how the microorganisms living in and around us influence the body. Our mission is to build a community where students can discover emerging microbiome research, connect with others who share their interests, and use what they learn to make healthier, informed choices for themselves!
gatorconnect.summary: Gator Microbiome educates students of all backgrounds about the microbiome and its connection to nutrition and overall health. Through engaging events, we empower students to explore microbiome science and make healthier, informed choices for themselves!

gatorconnect.description: GatorMDA is a student-run organization designed to fundraise for the Muscular Dystrophy Association. We aim to foster the values of community service, leadership, and youth activism. As a local chapter, we hold the same goals and values as those of the national organization.
gatorconnect.summary: GatorMDA is a student-run organization designed to fundraise for the Muscular Dystrophy Association. Our donations support funding research and hosting a week-long summer camp to provide kids with neuromuscular diseases normalcy and fun.

gatorconnect.description: Gator Neurobics is a student organization dedicated to exploring the connection between neuroscience and human movement through calisthenics. Rather than focusing solely on strength, repetition, or aesthetics, the organization emphasizes motor control, coordination, proprioception, and skill acquisition through structured bodyweight training. In addition to hands-on training, members participate in educational workshops, discussions, guest speakers, and interactive activities that explore topics such as motor learning, neural adaptation, movement, and human performance. By combining scientific concepts with practical application, members gain a deeper understanding of how the nervous system and body work together while developing new movement skills. Whether someone is completely new to calisthenics, interested in neuroscience, or simply looking to join a community that values learning and personal growth, Gator Neurobics welcomes students of all experience levels. Our mission is to create an environment where education, movement, and collaboration come together to help members better understand—and better control—the way they move.
gatorconnect.summary: A student organization that combines neuroscience and calisthenics through skill-based training, educational workshops, and community to develop motor control, coordination, proprioception, and a deeper understanding of human movement.

gatorconnect.summary: Gator of Tomorrow recognizes first year students at the University of Florida seeking to make major accomplishments both on campus and in the community.

gatorconnect.description: Here at Gator Robotics, we specialize in making combat robots (better known as battlebots) for competitions all around the United States. We currently build 1lb, 3lb, 12lb, and 30lb combat robots, allowing us to compete in almost every weight class of combat robots. Members are taught the ins and outs of robotics, starting from the design phase of the engineering design process, to fully creating and competing with their very own battlebot! Members gain real-world experience in CAD design, simulation, mechanical engineering, machining, and electronics through designing, building, and maintaining their own robot with help from the team. We mostly compete at regional competitions in Florida, but robots that are 3lbs and above get the chance to compete at the Norwalk Havoc Robot League in Connecticut.
gatorconnect.summary: Here at Gator Robotics, we specialize in helping you learn everything you need to know to build combat robots (aka Battlebots). We compete in local competitions as well as national competitions all around the US.

gatorconnect.description: Gator Strategy Group is a student-led venture consulting organization at the University of Florida that works with early-stage and technology-driven companies on strategic questions involving markets, growth, commercialization, operations, customer strategy, and other business priorities. Members work in small engagement teams and take direct responsibility for research, analysis, deliverable development, meeting preparation, client communication, and presenting findings when appropriate. Engagements are led by Engagement Managers and are designed to give members meaningful responsibility while developing judgment, critical thinking, communication, and ownership through the work itself. Beyond engagements, GSG invests in members through individualized professional development, career exploration, practitioner and founder conversations, recruiting preparation, mentorship, and access to opportunities across consulting, startups, venture capital, strategy, and related fields. The organization is built for students who want to take on demanding work, learn quickly, and grow alongside ambitious peers from a range of academic and professional backgrounds.

gatorconnect.description: We are a student-led organization dedicated to developing our own AI systems, particularly large language models (LLMs). Rather than relying solely on external APIs, we aim to develop and deploy in-house models for tasks such as natural language processing. Our long-term goals include designing our own embedding models, tokenizers, and neural network architectures, while researching tools to monitor and evaluate model behavior. Through this organization, we aim to educate members about the technologies underlying modern AI systems and prepare them to become innovators in AI models and algorithms rather than merely users of existing technologies. Members will work in specialized teams, including model training, data engineering, evaluation, and infrastructure. This structure will allow members to develop expertise in their areas while gaining hands-on experience with the techniques used by modern AI research organizations.
gatorconnect.summary: Building LLMs from the ground up to educate students about the inner workings of AI and deep learning technologies.

Combining quick wit and a penchant for being goofy, Generation has continued to deliver high-quality comedy to audiences every fall and spring semester. gatorconnect.description: Generational Relief in Prosthetics (GRiP) is a university-sponsored student organization dedicated to increasing accessibility and inclusion for children and teens with upper limb differences. Through community outreach, engineering, and education, GRiP designs and provides assistive devices at no cost to recipients and their families. These devices range from 3D-printed prosthetic hands to adapted gaming controllers and other customized technologies. GRiP partners with Hands to Love, a nonprofit organization that serves children and teens with upper limb differences. Throughout the year, student teams work directly on recipient projects, designing, manufacturing, and refining devices based on each individual’s needs. Each year, GRiP attends Hand Camp, where many of these completed devices are delivered to recipients who placed orders during the previous year. GRiP also hosts Adapt-a-thon, a large annual event focused on adapting toys for children with disabilities. During the event, members learn practical skills such as soldering and circuitry while modifying toys to make them more accessible. For example, students may replace small, difficult-to-use controls with larger external buttons. The adapted toys are then donated to nonprofit organizations such as Wheelchairs 4 Kids in time for the holiday season. In addition to these major outreach events, GRiP participates in the Assistive Technology Industry Association (ATIA) Conference in Orlando. Members share the organization’s work with families, assistive technology professionals, and other nonprofit organizations. Because GRiP provides its devices free of charge, the conference also provides an important opportunity to connect families with accessible alternatives in an assistive technology field that can otherwise be costly. Through engineering, education, and community partnerships, GRiP works to make assistive technology more accessible while providing university students with opportunities to develop technical skills in service of others. The organization continues to expand its efforts toward creating a more inclusive world for children and teens with upper limb differences.
gatorconnect.summary: GRiP teaches student engineers how to build assistive devise for real recipients, research and medical professionals.

Our organization is also built around helping others. Whether someone needs assistance navigating university life, finding housing, understanding local systems, dealing with an unexpected challenge, or simply needs someone to talk to, we strive to be there for them. We believe that a strong community is one where people support each other and no one feels alone. Our goal is to create a welcoming environment where every Bangladeshi student feels supported, connected, and at home. gatorconnect.description: Mock Lab is a creative agency led and operated by students that gives members real agency experience through collaborative mock campaigns, advertising, and branding.Our mission is to prepare students for the creative industry by providing opportunities to build professional portfolios, strengthen their skills, make meaningful connections, and explore different career paths within the creative field. Throughout the academic year, members will participate in networking events, portfolio workshops, campaign brainstorming sessions, and social gatherings that strengthen their creative skills, collaboration, and professional development. Members will also hear from professionals working in advertising, beauty and fashion, sports marketing, entertainment, social media, public relations, etc. These professionals will share their career advice, experiences, and industry knowledge with our members. Our mock campaigns are Mock Lab’s main focus. Throughout the semester, members will work in teams, take on roles based on their specific interests, and gain experience working in a creative agency environment. Each team will bring a campaign to life through research, strategy, branding, creative development, content production, and a final presentation. At the end of each academic year, the strongest campaigns will be featured in the professionally designed Mock Lab Campaign Magazine. The magazine will celebrate our members’ work and be shared with every guest speaker, as well as advertising agencies, marketing firms, brands, and other creative professionals. This gives our members the opportunity to have their work seen by people in the industry and make valuable professional connections.

gatorconnect.description: NeuroMusic is an interdisciplinary student organization dedicated to exploring the powerful connection between music, neuroscience, and medicine. Our mission is to educate students on the science behind music's effects on the brain, mental health, and patient healing while creating opportunities for research discussions, guest speakers, service initiatives, and student-led performances. Inspired by the healing impact of music in healthcare, NeuroMusic brings together students from all academic backgrounds who share an interest in medicine, neuroscience, psychology, music, and community service. Through collaborations with healthcare professionals, musicians, researchers, and local organizations, members gain a unique perspective on the role of music in patient care and neurological health. Beyond education, NeuroMusic is committed to giving back to the community by organizing fundraising events, benefit concerts, volunteer opportunities, and awareness campaigns that support pediatric neurological care through nonprofit organizations such as Children's Miracle Network . By combining science, creativity, and service, we strive to make a meaningful impact on both our campus and the patients and families we serve. Whether you're a musician, future healthcare professional, researcher, or simply passionate about the intersection of music and medicine, NeuroMusic welcomes you to join us in discovering where sound meets science.

gatorconnect.description: The North African Student Association (NASA) at the University of Florida was established in Spring 2025 to create a dedicated community for students of North African descent and those interested in the region’s rich heritage. We are dedicated to showcasing the unique tapestry of North African identity, raising awareness of our culture's distinct traditions while highlighting the incredible diversity within our community. Above all, NASA is committed to providing a welcoming, inclusive space on campus where students can easily connect, find unity, and share their experiences. To bring our heritage to life, we host interactive cultural workshops, hands-on craft events, food showcases, and lively social gatherings, while also coordinating fundraisers and advocacy events to support humanitarian causes in our region. Whether you are looking to reconnect with your roots or want to experience something new, NASA opens its doors to members of all backgrounds.

gatorconnect.description: We are a chapter of NAYGN Intercontinental, whose mission is to develop leadership and professional skills among young nuclear enthusiasts, engage the public, and inspire the next generation of industry professionals. As a chapter, we benefit from Intercontinental resources such as conference scholarships, 1:1 professional mentorship, and opportunities to serve on intercontinental committees that shape initiatives across all NAYGN chapters. Our Public Information Committee leads outreach for Nuclear Science Week and Earth Week, organizes our annual Hill Day in Tallahassee, coordinates postcard pushes and social media campaigns, and works to share the benefits of peaceful nuclear technology with communities who may be hearing about it for the first time. Our Professional Development Committee hosts industry speakers, runs LinkedIn and résumé workshops, builds an internship bank, conducts mock interviews, and coordinates UF reactor tours to help members strengthen their professional skills and explore career paths in the nuclear sector. We welcome all majors—if you’re excited about nuclear’s role in energy, medicine, agriculture, or space, there’s a place for you here. Visit our website to learn how to join and see our upcoming events.
gatorconnect.summary: We believe in nuclear for peace, from clean energy to lifesaving medicine, resilient agriculture, and space exploration. Anyone excited to share nuclear with others can join our committees, drive our outreach, and grow leadership skills along the way.

gatorconnect.description: ONWARD is a first-year student organization built on the belief that students should actively shape their college experience rather than simply participate in one created for them. Our organization provides first-year students with a community where they can explore new interests, develop personally, form meaningful connections, and gain confidence navigating the University of Florida while taking an active role in building the experiences they want to have. Unlike organizations centered primarily around predetermined programming, ONWARD is driven directly by its members. Members are encouraged to develop, plan, and host their own events, activities, and “side quests” based on what they want to experience, learn, or share with others. These may range from exploring Gainesville and trying new activities to service projects, recreational events, skill-sharing, personal development opportunities, and spontaneous group experiences. Members have the opportunity to turn an idea into an experience for the entire community, allowing them to practice initiative, collaboration, communication, creativity, and leadership in an approachable environment. ONWARD also helps first-year students build connections beyond the organization by introducing them to upperclassmen, student leaders, campus resources, organizations, and potential mentors who align with their interests and goals. Rather than assigning every student the same path, we aim to help members identify the people, experiences, and opportunities that can support the direction they choose for themselves. Through active membership, peer-led experiences, mentorship, and exploration, ONWARD gives first-year students the space to learn by doing. Members are not simply attendees, they are contributors who help determine what the organization becomes. In doing so, ONWARD aims to help students develop a greater sense of independence, belonging, and ownership over their college experience from the very beginning.
gatorconnect.summary: ONWARD helps first-year students navigate college through mentorship, personal development, community, and exploration. Through member-led experiences and campus "side quests," students build connections, discover opportunities, and grow together.

Occasionally, it also hosts resume reviews, guest speakers from tech companies, and competitive hackathons.
gatorconnect.summary: The Open Source Club (OSC) at the University of Florida is a community of makers who want to solve problems and improve our world through open source projects.

gatorconnect.summary: The goal of Outdoor Adventure Recreation (OAR) is to make outdoor activities, including hiking, camping, backpacking, rock climbing, and paddling, easily accessible to the UF community through weekly trips and outdoor skills clinics.

gatorconnect.summary: The purpose of OUTdoors is to carve out a safe and affirming space for all students, including LGBTQ+ and feminine-presenting or -identifying individuals.

gatorconnect.description: Partners in Health Engage supports global healthcare access through three pillars: advocacy, fundraising, and community building and education. In regards to advocacy, for instance, we schedule virtual meetings with the offices of Members of Congress in order to discuss critical global health legislation and take direct action. Partners in Health Engage operates under the umbrella of the international organization Partners in Health, which supports healthcare access across multiple countries by providing resources, medical training and education, and the construction of healthcare facilities. Our fundraising efforts all go towards supporting these endeavors.
gatorconnect.summary: We are a chapter of the national network Partners in Health Engage, which is a grassroots organization committed to supporting global healthcare access through advocacy, fundraising, and community building and education.

gatorconnect.description: Passionate Musicians on Call is a service-based organization at the University of Florida. Our mission is to provid e musical performances to underserved communities in Gainesville to address the social determinants of health. Music is well-known for providing potential well-being and health benefits by encouraging social connection, emotional release, and alleviating stress. Our target populations include individuals who are low-income, elderly, homeless, disabled, immigrants, socially disadvantaged, and/or chronically ill. The goal is to have a variety of musical groups such as Orchestra, Symphonic, Jazz, and Choir ensembles where members play together for the audience in groups, as well as solo performances. Members also engage in socials, outreach events, and general body meetings.
gatorconnect.summary: Passionate Musicians on Call is a UF student group that shares live music with Gainesville’s underserved communities. We perform diverse genres for elderly, low-income, chronically ill, and disadvantaged individuals, fostering connection and joy.

gatorconnect.description: PERIOD. at UF is a student-led chapter of PERIOD., a global youth-powered nonprofit dedicated to ending period poverty and menstrual stigma through advocacy, education, and service. The UF chapter works to promote menstrual equity on campus and in the surrounding community by increasing access to period products, raising awareness about menstrual health, providing educational opportunities, and supporting initiatives that challenge the stigma surrounding menstruation. Through community service, educational programming, product drives, and advocacy, PERIOD. at UF aims to ensure that menstruation is never a barrier to education, participation, or well-being. The chapter empowers students to become advocates for menstrual equity while connecting the University of Florida community with the broader movement to make menstrual products accessible, menstrual health education more comprehensive, and conversations about periods more inclusive and stigma-free.
gatorconnect.summary: PERIOD. at the University of Florida is a student-led organization advancing menstrual equity through period product drives, educational initiatives, community service, and advocacy to reduce period poverty and menstrual stigma.

gatorconnect.summary: PERMIAS Gainesville is a student-led organization that brings together Indonesian students for cultural, social, educational, and community activities in Gainesville.

gatorconnect.summary: Personal Finance Club helps students build financial literacy through topics like budgeting, investing, and personal wealth management. Weekly meetings and guest speakers provide practical insights and opportunities to connect with industry professionals
The purpose of this Pharmacy Student Council- Gainesville is to unite the faculty, different campuses, students, and all of the student organizations in the college.

gatorconnect.description: We are an engineering social sorority fostering lifelong friendships, professional connections, and a commitment to serving the community. We host semesterly retreats and banquets, organize fundraisers for service projects and our philanthropy, The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society, and welcome industry professionals to share career insights and advice. Beyond social events, our members support one another academically by sharing knowledge about classes, work opportunities, and navigating engineering coursework. Older members mentor younger sisters, who in turn pass that guidance on to future generations, creating a lasting culture of support. Every sister gets the chance to contribute her unique strengths in meaningful ways while building friendships that extend far beyond graduation. Policy Advocacy in Science and Engineering is not an organization involved in politics, litigation, or lobbying. gatorconnect.summary: Pre-Dental Society is an undergraduate organization that unites students through excellence in service, education, and engagement while exploring the field of dentistry. We provide networking, community service and professional development opportunities.

gatorconnect.description: Prestigious Awards Student Support (PASS the Torch) is a student-led organization at the University of Florida dedicated to making prestigious scholarships, fellowships, grants, and other competitive opportunities more visible and accessible to students. PASS the Torch supports students at every stage of the process—from discovering opportunities that align with their academic and professional goals to understanding what makes a competitive application and developing the confidence to apply. gatorconnect.description: Product Space at the University of Florida Product Space at UF was founded to fill a gap in university resources for students interested in product careers. The organization provides education, curriculum, and hands-on opportunities in three core areas: Product Management, Product Marketing, and Product Design. We aim to help members build both the technical skills and professional network needed to break into the product field. Vision The chapter's vision is to empower and professionally develop UF's product community by offering high-quality resources, meaningful connections, and real-world experience. Programs & Structure General Body Meetings: Organization-wide gatherings aimed to spread awareness about the industry and openly provide resources. Fellowship Program: A structured curriculum run across three verticals (Product Management, Product Marketing, and Product Design), each led by a dedicated Director of Fellowship who teaches weekly sessions and oversees interdisciplinary capstone projects. gatorconnect.description: Professional Pathways in Economics (PPE) is a student organization dedicated to helping economics students confidently transition from the classroom to their careers. While the economics curriculum develops strong analytical and critical thinking skills, many students graduate without the professional network, industry exposure, or career guidance needed to navigate the wide range of opportunities available to them. PPE exists to bridge that gap. Our mission is to complement the academic experience by connecting students with the people, resources, and experiences that prepare them for professional success. Through speaker panels featuring alumni and industry professionals, career development workshops, peer office hours, and a mentorship ambassador program, PPE provides students with practical insight into careers in consulting, finance, public policy, strategy, graduate education, and other economics-related fields. PPE primarily serves undergraduate economics students, particularly underclassmen who are beginning to explore career options and build their professional foundation. Members gain access to mentorship, networking opportunities, and actionable guidance on topics such as resumes, interviewing, internships, and professional communication, while developing meaningful relationships with peers, faculty, alumni, and employers. By creating a supportive community centered on career exploration and professional growth, PPE empowers students to make informed decisions about their futures and graduate with the confidence, connections, and skills needed to succeed. In doing so, the organization advances the University of Florida’s commitment to developing knowledgeable, engaged, and career-ready graduates.
gatorconnect.summary: Professional Pathways in Economics (PPE) prepares economics students for careers beyond graduation. Through mentorship, professional development, speaker panels, and industry engagement, PPE bridges the gap between classroom learning and career readiness

gatorconnect.description: The purpose of the Programming Team is to provide a collaborative and educational platform for students interested in computer programming and problem-solving. Our primary goals are: 1. Skills Development: To foster the growth of programming skills, algorithmic thinking, and problem-solving abilities among our members. 2. Competition Excellence: To prepare and empower our members to excel in programming competitions, with a particular focus on participation in the International Collegiate Programming Competition (ICPC) and similar events. This includes active participation in the yearly Southeast Regional ICPC competition and the potential for further competitions based on performance in the regionals. 3. Teamwork and Collaboration: To cultivate a culture of teamwork and collaboration, allowing members to work together to tackle complex problems and learn from each other's experiences. 4. Community Engagement: To engage with the University of Florida community and the broader programming community by organizing workshops, seminars, and coding challenges that promote knowledge sharing and networking. 5. Events and Activities: To host a variety of programming-related events, including practice contests, coding bootcamps, guest speaker sessions, and hackathons, providing valuable opportunities for skill enhancement and practical experience. By offering a range of services, events, and programs, the Programming Team aims to create a dynamic and enriching environment that not only enhances the technical capabilities of its members but also contributes positively to the campus and programming communities at large. Through our dedication to competitions like the Southeast Regional ICPC and the potential for further achievements, we strive to showcase the excellence and prowess of our members in the field of programming.
gatorconnect.summary: The purpose of the Programming Team is to provide a collaborative and educational platform for students interested in computer programming and problem-solving.

gatorconnect.description: At the core of Project Common Table, we focus on an initiative-based approach to homelessness prevention and rehousing efforts. This means that direct action such as rapid-rehousing and community rebuilding through volunteerism is the main way we intend to decrease homelessness. While we will focus on volunteering to accomplish our mission, we also intend to make education an important aspect of our mission. Such education includes equity vs. equality, the importance of government support in rehousing efforts, and the impact substance (ab)use can have on homelessness. These educational experiences can be accomplished through guest speakers, team building activities, and short lectures at general body meetings.
gatorconnect.summary: The mission of Project Common Table is to directly and holistically combat homelessness through community outreach and involvement, fundraising campaigns, recovery programs, and various homelessness prevention efforts.

gatorconnect.description: Project Makeover at UF is a student-led organization dedicated to transforming local elementary schools into more engaging and inspiring learning environments. Founded at the University of Florida in 2008, Project Makeover brings together UF students and community members to improve school campuses through service and creativity. Each year, the organization selects a local elementary school and organizes a large-scale makeover weekend involving more than 1,000 volunteers. Projects include painting interactive murals, landscaping, completing a Dream Project requested by the school, and making other improvements to the campus. Through these efforts, Project Makeover aims to create learning spaces that inspire imagination, confidence, joy, and a sense of belonging among students. Members have opportunities to participate in volunteering, fundraising, community outreach, and the planning and execution of the annual makeover.
gatorconnect.summary: Project Makeover at UF brings students and community members together to transform local elementary schools through murals, construction projects, landscaping, and other improvements that create inspiring and engaging learning environments.

gatorconnect.description: The University of Florida’s Public Relations Student Society of America (UF PRSSA) Alpha Chapter was founded on April 4, 1968, as one of the nine original PRSSA chapters, making it the oldest public relations organization at the University of Florida. As a pre-professional organization, UF PRSSA is dedicated to preparing students for successful careers in public relations and related communications fields by providing opportunities to build industry knowledge, professional skills, and meaningful connections. UF PRSSA’s mission is to serve its members by enhancing their understanding of public relations through innovative professional development opportunities and hands-on experiences. The chapter fosters a collaborative environment where students can learn from one another, connect with public relations professionals, and explore the many career paths available within the industry. Members have access to a variety of benefits, including networking opportunities with industry professionals, professional development events, conferences and travel opportunities, exclusive internship opportunities, and opportunities to learn about different sectors of public relations. Members can also receive reduced rates for PRSA memberships and gain valuable connections that can support their professional growth beyond college. Through its commitment to collaboration, professional development, and lasting relationships, UF PRSSA empowers students to gain the knowledge, experience, and confidence needed to transition from the classroom into the public relations profession.

gatorconnect.description: QuantED at the University of Florida QuantED makes quantitative finance accessible to any UF student who is curious about it, regardless of major or background. Quant work sits at the intersection of math, statistics, computer science, and markets, and most students never get a clear picture of it until they are already competing for internships. We close that gap. What we do Lecture series. Our core programming is a recurring lecture series built for students new to the space, covering markets and derivatives, how systematic strategies are researched and tested, and the technical skills firms screen for. Workshops and speakers. We bring in practitioners and faculty for hands-on sessions and honest conversations about how they got into the field. Gator Quant Hacks. Each year QuantED hosts a national quantitative finance competition at UF, open to students across the country, with industry sponsors, judges from leading firms, and tracks spanning research, quantitative puzzles, and systematic trading. Career preparation. Resume reviews, interview structure, and guidance on which skills to build first. Who should join Anyone. Math, statistics, CS, economics, finance, and engineering students will find the material familiar, but no prior finance experience is assumed. Come to one lecture or help us run the club.
gatorconnect.summary: QuantED introduces UF students to quantitative finance through a beginner-friendly lecture series, hands-on workshops, and Gator Quant Hacks, our national quant competition. No prior background needed.

gatorconnect.description: Reformed University Fellowship ("RUF") is a Christian ministry to college students from all walks of life. We are affiliated with the Presbyterian Church in America, but we minister to students from all backgrounds: both the "convinced" and the "unconvinced". We believe that the gospel speaks to the whole person, and that it can transform any place, bringing the healing and restoration of Christ's Kingdom. gatorconnect.description: SCOPE at the University of Florida is the local chapter of SCOPE USA, a national nonprofit organization focused on strengthening public safety through community-driven innovation. Our mission is to empower students to apply engineering, technology, and interdisciplinary problem-solving to real challenges facing first responders and local communities. Members collaborate on hands-on projects such as emergency response technologies, disaster preparedness tools, communications systems, robotics, drones, software, and other open-source solutions designed to improve community resilience. In addition to technical project development, the organization connects students with industry and public safety professionals through mentorship, provides opportunities for outreach and STEM education, and partners with local organizations to create meaningful real-world impact. SCOPE welcomes students from all majors who are passionate about using their skills to serve their communities, regardless of prior technical experience.
