gatorconnect.description: Sigma Phi Lambda - Sisters for the Lord, is a nondenominational Christian Sorority outside of the Panhellenic Council. Our sole purpose is to glorify God and make His name great, we do so by fostering a community of women who seek to grow in their faith, serve others, and support one another through Christ-centered sisterhood. While we share many of the elements found in traditional Greek life—such as chapter meetings, big/little, formals, philanthropy, socials, service, and retreats—Sigma Phi Lambda is distinct in that we are founded on Christian values. gatorconnect.description: Structural Graduate Student Seminar (SGSS) is a Student Organization operating within the Department of Civil and Coastal Engineering at the University of Florida. Our core activity is a regular seminar series in which graduate students prepare and deliver technical presentations on their own research. Every dollar we collect goes towards supporting cancer research initiatives such as the American Cancer Society and Pancreatic Cancer Action Network. What sets us apart is our commitment to donating 100% of our profits to the cause. We firmly believe that together, as a community, we can make a significant impact in the fight against cancer.
gatorconnect.summary: Raise money and provide UF Students with volunteer opportunities to help the fight against cancer.

gatorconnect.description: Students Against Infection is a student organization dedicated to promoting awareness, education, and service related to infectious diseases and infection prevention. Our mission is to create opportunities for students to learn about the impact of infectious diseases on individuals and communities while encouraging practical approaches to prevention, public health, and health education. The organization brings together students interested in healthcare, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, microbiology, research, public health, and community service. Through educational events, guest speakers, workshops, outreach programs, service projects, and collaborations with other organizations, members can expand their understanding of infectious disease while becoming more involved in the UF and Gainesville communities. Gators Against Infection also aims to make complex public health topics more accessible by providing students with opportunities to discuss disease transmission, prevention strategies, antimicrobial resistance, vaccination, emerging infections, and other issues affecting public health. Our organization is open to students of all majors and years, regardless of previous experience. We hope to build a welcoming community where members can develop leadership and communication skills, participate in meaningful service, explore healthcare and public health interests, and work together to promote healthier communities. By combining education, outreach, and service, Gators Against Infection seeks to empower students to make a positive impact both on campus and beyond.
gatorconnect.summary: Students Against Infection is a UF student organization focused on infection prevention, infectious disease education, public health awareness, community outreach, and service.

gatorconnect.summary: Students Demand Action is established for the expressed purpose of organizing students at The University of Florida to advocate for sensible gun legislation.

gatorconnect.description: Students Eat Right's main goal is to provide nutrition education for University of Florida students and the local Gainesville community. Previous meetings have highlighted the importance of nutrition in various areas of health, such as nutrition's role in the menstrual cycle and the benefits of probiotics. Each month, the organization hosts events typically centered around national nutrition holidays or pressing health issues within the local community, such as walks supporting breast cancer research. The club also strives to promote nutrition advocacy by incorporating nutrition-focused organizations, such as WIC, into monthly meetings and educational initiatives.
gatorconnect.summary: Students Eat Right is a club dedicated to providing nutrition education through educational meetings and interactive events. The organization also promotes nutrition advocacy and raises awareness about the dietetics profession.

gatorconnect.description: Students for a National Healthcare Plan (SNaHP) is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing healthcare advocacy, promoting health equity, and empowering future healthcare professionals to create a more just and accessible healthcare system. Through education, community engagement, policy discussions, and service initiatives, we foster meaningful conversations about the social, economic, and structural factors that shape health outcomes. As a student chapter affiliated with Physicians for a National Health Program (PNHP), we support evidence-based healthcare reform, including Medicare for All, while maintaining a broader mission of inspiring students to advocate for equitable, patient-centered care and lasting improvements in healthcare for all communities.
gatorconnect.summary: Students for a National Healthcare Plan (SNaHP) is a student organization dedicated to promoting healthcare advocacy, advancing health equity, and educating future healthcare professionals about the policies and systems that shape patient care.

gatorconnect.description: Students for Justice in Palestine at the University of Florida is a student-led human rights advocacy organization dedicated to advancing advocacy, awareness, education, and collective action in support of Palestinian rights and self-determination. Grounded in international law and universal human rights, we challenge the ongoing Israeli occupation of Palestine and work to foster meaningful engagement within our university and broader community. We are committed to justice, dignity, equality, and self-determination for Palestinians and all peoples subjected to oppression, dispossession, and systems of inequality. We believe that meaningful change requires active engagement and collective responsibility, and we seek to build intersectional solidarity among communities and movements working against oppression in all of its forms. Our organization welcomes a diverse membership of people of all faiths, nationalities, and backgrounds who share a commitment to human rights and collective liberation.
gatorconnect.summary: The UF branch of Students for Justice in Palestine is a diverse network of students advocating for Palestinian liberation and rights through activism, community aid, cultural practice, and political and historical education.

Students for Kahf seeks to promote and raise awareness about Students for Kahf, a local non-profit aimed at providing community, knowledge, and spiritual connection for Muslim young adults in Gainesville, Florida.

We exist to make disciples who make disciples of Jesus Christ. We are also affiliated with The Salt Company (“TSC”), a college ministry of Salt Church. gatorconnect.summary: Students for Salt is a faith-based UF organization creating community through events and spaces where students can connect, grow, and experience a glimpse of Christ-centered community.

gatorconnect.description: Capitalism has proven to be a system that exploits and creates misery for the working-class, while solely benefiting the elite ruling class. As students, faculty members, and people of the community in general, we believe in the replacement of this system of capitalism with the implementation of a socialist economy. We believe capitalism, its later stage of imperialism, in which we currently live, is inherently racist, sexist, oppressive, exploitative, and unable to fulfill and guarantee the needs of all people. We support all movements against US imperialism, revolutionary national liberation movements, and so forth. We support a nation's right to self-determination. We support democratic centralism as a form of organization. We believe a revolutionary party made up by the working-class, for the working-class, is necessary for unity in the struggle for socialism. We believe in socialism: a system where private property is nationalized by the working-class state, a system where the working-class, all oppressed and marginalized people are in control of the means of production and property in general. Students for Socialism, SFS, stands behind these goals wholly. We are a revolutionary Marxist-Leninist student organization.
gatorconnect.summary: We are a revolutionary Marxist student group at the University of Florida, organizing for the replacement of capitalism with socialism.

SSI actively supports the State of Israel and believes in the right for the Jewish State to exist.
gatorconnect.summary: The mission of Students Supporting Israel (SSI) is to be a clear and confident pro-Israel voice on college campuses and to support students in grassroots pro-Israel advocacy.

With our centralized location, we have a culture of travel and “strike missions”, ranging anywhere from nearby St Augustine to New Smyrna, SoCal, Nicaragua, and beyond. gatorconnect.summary: Surf Club is a RecSports organization that focuses on spreading the stoke all throughout Gainesville and the state of Florida by hosting events based on action, culture, and sport. We also have a nationally-competitive surf team.

At UF, we work on a variety of initiatives, including monthly beach and local cleanups, community outreach and education focused on ocean conservation and sustainability, and policy advocacy at the state and national levels. We also strive to build a welcoming community where members can make lifelong friendships and connect with others who share a passion for the environment. Our club balances meaningful environmental advocacy with fun and engaging social events, including concerts, game nights, and other activities. Whether you're interested in environmental activism, marine conservation, community outreach, or simply want to meet like-minded people, Surfrider at UF offers opportunities to get involved and make a difference.
gatorconnect.summary: The Surfrider Foundation is dedicated to the protection and enjoyment of the world’s ocean, waves, and beaches, for all people, through a powerful activist network.

gatorconnect.description: Founded in 2019, the Swamp Launch Rocket Team exists as student organization encompassing University of Florida students from a wide range of backgrounds and majors. Formally known as The University of Florida Rocket Team, Swamp Launch enables students to study, engineer, and launch high-powered rockets. The team is not only dedicated to participating in nationwide rocketry competitions but has also devoted abundant effort into educating its members and local community. The Swamp Launch Rocket Team competes in the Intercollegiate Rocket Engineering Competition (IREC). Aside from competitions, members have the opportunity to earn their high-powered rocket (HPR) certifications through the National Association of Rocketry (NAR) by designing and building their own rockets with tools, materials, and knowledge provided by Swamp Launch. The team also hosts courses to teach the basics of rockets and inspire a passion for rocketry in newer members. Community outreach is another major part of our mission as we strive to inspire the next generation of engineers by attending local schools and hosting STEM-related activities. Currently, we are split into three main groups, each dedicated to a part of the competition the Intercollegiate Rocket Engineering Competition (IREC). Our first group is dedicated to the development of a competition launch vehicle. Our second group is tasked with engineering a payload to complete some designated requirements set by the team. Our last group is focused on development projects that allow us to progress to further levels in the competition and reach towards our long term goal of a spaceshot. Each group is further divided into sub-teams that focus on specific parts of the rocket such as avionics, recovery, modeling and simulation, payloads, structures, and testing.
gatorconnect.summary: Swamp Launch Rocket Team is an award-winning student design team at the University of Florida that enables students to design, build, and launch high-powered rockets. We are devoted to educating our members and community about rocketry.

gatorconnect.description: Swamp Records is a student-run independent record label and artist resource organization based in Gainesville at the University of Florida. Our artists have earned spots at major festivals and played all over the country. We have had the privilege of working with notable acts like flipturn, SALES, Tessa Violet, Last Dinosaurs, Magic City Hippies, Sister Hazel, The Happy Fits, and Early Eyes, further solidifying our impact on the regional music scene. As of Fall 2025, our artists have performed shows in New York City and Los Angeles, California. Our primary mission is to provide opportunities for UF students seeking music industry experience. The interests and well-being of our members come before our artists. We provide marketing, public relations, advertising, web development, and booking services to musicians and bands, while offering students valuable, hands-on experience in the music industry. Our teams need to elevate, reassess, and realign our strategies regularly to keep up with the fast-paced industry and marketing needs.
gatorconnect.summary: Gainesville's student-run label and artist resource agency. We provide management, marketing/PR, web development, and booking services to musicians throughout central Florida, while offering students valuable, hands-on experience in the music industry.

For over fifteen years, members have volunteered their time and talents to present this event, which celebrates art, fashion, gaming, pop culture, cosplay, and performance arts across fandoms. SwampCon is family friendly, and open to everybody–whether you’re a student, a Gainesville local, or from halfway across the world! What to Expect: student made Miku Concert (hologram concert), IdolFest, Lip Sync Competition, Cosplay Competition, Maid Cafe, panels, local artists and vendors, guests, and game room

gatorconnect.description: Welcome to Sweets4Hope! Whether you love baking, enjoy cooking, want to give back to the community, need volunteer or service hours, or simply want to meet people who are passionate about making a difference, Sweets4Hope is the organization for you. Our mission is to support Gainesville's growing homeless population through service, compassion, and community outreach. We believe that even small acts of kindness can have a lasting impact, and we provide students with meaningful opportunities to serve their community while building friendships with like-minded individuals. Throughout the semester, members work together to fundraise, with all proceeds going toward purchasing ingredients and supplies for meal preparation. During our general body meetings, members prepare and assemble homemade meals that are distributed directly to individuals experiencing homelessness, while also partnering with local shelters and outreach organizations to expand our impact. No baking or cooking experience is required—everyone is welcome. Whether you want to volunteer occasionally or become more involved through official membership and leadership opportunities, every contribution helps us provide hope, one meal at a time.
gatorconnect.summary: S4H empowers students to make a difference by preparing and distributing homemade meals to Gainesville’s homeless community. Through hands-on service and fundraising, S4H fosters compassion, service, and community engagement.

Also, we are planning to share Taiwanese culture, including traditional foods, festivals and language with people who might not be familiar with Taiwan. Annually, we have three main events: the tubing event, autumn festival, and Chinese new year. By hosting and participating in these events, students can experience Taiwanese culture in person, know UF more with Taiwanese peers and build up a network with international students.
gatorconnect.summary: In this organization, we are dedicated to making a connection with Taiwanese students on campus. Also, we are planning to share Taiwanese culture, including traditional foods, festivals and language with people who might not be familiar with Taiwan.

gatorconnect.description: The Florida TAMID chapter was founded in 2013. It currently has over 100 members and alumni from diverse academic backgrounds. Some of our members have worked at Goldman Sachs, McKinsey & Company, P&G, and Ernst and Young! The TAMID Education track aims to develop members professionally, help them understand the various facets of the entrepreneurship world, and help them analyze the factors behind Israel’s accession as a startup and tech powerhouse. The track also teaches members skills in preparation for the Consulting and Investment Fund tracks. The TAMID Consulting track allows our members to provide consulting for the most exciting and innovative companies coming out of Israel. TAMID members engage in projects during the academic year that build skills in market research, competitive analysis, US market entry strategy, beta testing/product development and design, and more. The TAMID Investment Fund track leverages a partnership with Seeking Alpha to develop strong equity research skills while all TAMID chapters compete in a national fund competition that decides which companies will be added to the national TAMID stock portfolio. Lastly, the TAMID Fellowship is a unique opportunity over the summer that allows members to live in Israel for eight weeks and work at high-tech groundbreaking startups and gain first-hand experience in the start-up nation.
gatorconnect.summary: TAMID is a non-religious organization that aims to train the next generation of entrepreneurs through a comprehensive education curriculum, pro-bono consulting for Israeli startups, capital market investment research, and a summer fellowship in Israel.

gatorconnect.description: Tau Beta Pi is the principal engineering honor society, originally founded in 1885 and having initiated over 650,000 members to date. Our purpose is to recognize exceptional engineering students, promote academic and professional excellence, encourage young students to pursue engineering, and serve our local community. Additionally, Tau Beta Pi offers exclusive opportunities for networking and scholarship awards within the society. The Florida Alpha Chapter was established in 1961, and out of 259 collegiate chapters, is one of the nation's most active. We have been named the Most Outstanding Chapter 10 times. To be eligible for membership, juniors must be in the top eighth of their class, and seniors and graduate students must be in the top fifth of their class; all candidates must demonstrate exemplary character.
gatorconnect.summary: Tau Beta Pi is the principal engineering honor society, originally founded in 1885. We are committed to the academic, professional, and personal development of students across all fields of engineering through leadership and serving our community.

gatorconnect.description: The Belly Gators are the University of Florida's premier belly dance troupe, dedicated to the art, culture, and community of belly dance. We welcome dancers of every skill level, from beginners to experienced performers, in a supportive space that celebrates growth and self-expression. Members explore traditional Middle Eastern belly dance and fusion styles through weekly practices, workshops, and choreography sessions, building both technical skill and genuine community. Throughout the year, the troupe performs at campus events, cultural showcases, and community gatherings, sharing the artistry of belly dance with Gainesville.
gatorconnect.summary: UF's premier belly dance troupe, uniting dancers of every level through the art and community of Middle Eastern dance.

gatorconnect.description: The Bilingual Brain is a student organization dedicated to promoting brain health, dementia and Alzheimer's disease awareness, and culturally responsive community engagement. Our mission is to educate students and the community on the role of bilingualism, lifelong learning, and cognitive engagement in supporting healthy brain aging while addressing health disparities in underserved populations. Through educational meetings , service initiatives , fundraising , and community outreach , members translate neuroscience research into meaningful action. Our signature programming includes bilingual cognitive enrichment activities, dementia awareness campaigns, and partnerships with community organizations serving older adults. We also host educational events that explore topics such as cognitive reserve, language and the brain, Alzheimer's disease, and culturally competent healthcare. The Bilingual Brain welcomes students from all majors who are passionate about neuroscience, medicine, psychology, public health, linguistics, education, and community service. Whether members hope to pursue careers in healthcare or simply want to make a positive impact, our organization provides opportunities to learn, lead, advocate, and serve while promoting healthier communities through science, education, and compassion.
gatorconnect.summary: The Bilingual Brain educates and empowers UF students to promote dementia and Alzheimer's prevention through bilingual outreach, brain health education, and culturally responsive service to underserved communities.

gatorconnect.summary: The Billy Mitchell Drill Team is a premier drill, ceremony, and color guard team. With a history spanning over 75 years, the Billy Mitchell Drill Team's rich heritage, dedication to discipline, and excellence, help to develop successful leaders.

canonical_name: The Federalist Society for Law and Public Policy Studies

gatorconnect.description: The Federalist Society for Law and Public Policy Studies is a group of conservatives and libertarians interested in the current state of the legal order. It is founded on the principles that the state exists to preserve freedom, that the separation of governmental powers is central to our Constitution, and that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be. The Society seeks both to promote an awareness of these principles and to further their application through its activities. On the Law School Campus, the goal of the society is to promote civil disagreement and elevate legal discourse by introducing students to traditional conservative perspectives on legal issues via panels and debates. The society does not take specific policy positions or promote specific political outcomes, but stresses the importance of debate, thoughtful discussion, and well-reasoned decisionmaking.
gatorconnect.summary: The Federalist Society for Law and Public Policy Studies is founded on the principle that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be.

canonical_name: The Florida Chapter of Alpha Zeta

gatorconnect.description: Founded in 1897 at The Ohio State University, Alpha Zeta is the first and oldest collegiate society for agriculture. We take pride in our commitment to the highest levels of scholarship, leadership, integrity and service. The Florida Chapter of Alpha Zeta is the largest in the nation. Our chapter is involved in campus events as well as service, social, and fundraising opportunities. Each fall and spring semester, students who are academically in the top 40% of the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences are invited to join.
gatorconnect.summary: Alpha Zeta is an honorary, professional society for students and industry professionals in the agriculture and natural resources fields.

gatorconnect.summary: The purpose of The Fossil Record (TFR) is to ignite and nurture a passion for paleontology among University of Florida students from all academic backgrounds. We aim to demystify the study of fossils, making it accessible and engaging for everyone.

gatorconnect.description: The Surprise Guys is an organization dedicated to empowering single mothers and children from foster homes through surprise appreciation events that celebrate their strength, resilience, and worth. We believe that the women and children who carry some of life's heaviest burdens deserve moments of unexpected joy, recognition, and community support. Through thoughtfully planned surprise events, we bring a sense of dignity and celebration to those who are too often overlooked — reminding them that they are not alone, and that their courage does not go unnoticed. Every surprise is designed to uplift, encourage, and create lasting memories for families who need it most. To deepen our impact, The Surprise Guys partners with respected local nonprofit organizations such as One More Child and Girls Place, working alongside them to identify families and children who would benefit most from our appreciation events. These partnerships allow us to reach the community more effectively, ensure our efforts are aligned with the real needs on the ground, and build a stronger network of support for single mothers and foster children in our area.
gatorconnect.summary: The Surprise Guys is an organization dedicated to empowering single mothers and children from foster care through surprise appreciation events that celebrate their strength and remind them they are valued.

gatorconnect.description: The Warrington Veterans Association (WVA) is dedicated to serving veteran and military-affiliated students throughout their collegiate journey and beyond. WVA exists to ensure that no veteran student navigates the business school experience alone, and that the skills, discipline, and leadership forged through military service are recognized, developed, and connected to meaningful careers in business. WVA operates across five lines of effort: building community for veterans and military-affiliated students within Warrington and the broader UF ecosystem; translating military skills and experience into recognized assets for civilian business careers; creating a pipeline of veteran-friendly companies that actively recruit Warrington veterans for leadership roles; serving as veteran ambassadors for Warrington admissions to grow the incoming military-affiliated student population; and building a sustainable organization with lasting institutional presence that serves Gator veterans well beyond the founding class. Members of WVA gain access to a peer network of fellow veterans navigating the same transition, direct connections to veteran-friendly employers through partnerships with Warrington's Business Career Services, a dedicated transition support resource repository covering programs such as Hiring Our Heroes, American Corporate Partners, and Deloitte CORE, and an informal connection to the UF Association of Military Alumni (UFAMA) that extends WVA's network beyond graduation. Programming includes community and social events, career development panels and employer recruiting nights, veteran ambassador outreach in coordination with Warrington admissions, joint programming with other UF veteran programs, and community service events supporting the Gainesville veteran community. Membership is open to all military-affiliated graduate students enrolled at the Warrington College of Business, including veterans, active duty service members, reservists, members of the National Guard, ROTC participants, military spouses, dependents, and all other military affiliated students. Students with a demonstrated commitment to supporting the veteran community are welcome to participate as associate members. Leadership opportunities are available across ten positions, including four constitutional officer roles and six appointed director positions covering Communications, Corporate Relations, Events, Membership, Alumni and Veteran Outreach, and Transition Support. If you are a Gator veteran or military-affiliated student at Warrington, this is your organization. Come build something that lasts.
gatorconnect.summary: The WVA builds community for Gator veterans and military-affiliated students at Warrington College of Business through camaraderie, career development, veteran-friendly employer partnerships, and transition support.

gatorconnect.description: Wishmakers on Campus grants wishes to children with life-threatening medical conditions. A wish experience can be a game-changer for a child with a life-threatening medical condition and costs on average $10,000 for just one wish. Wishes are more than just a nice thing. This one belief guides us in everything we. It inspires us to grant wishes that change the lives of the kids we serve. It compels us to be creative in exceeding the expectations of every wish kid. It drives us to make our donated resources go as far as possible. Most of all, it's the founding principle of our vision to grant the wish of every eligible child. Wishes are far more than gifts, or singular events in time. Wishes impact everyone involved - wish kids, volunteers, donors, sponsors, medical professionals and communities. The impact varies. For wish kids, just the act of making their wish come true can give them the courage to comply with their medical treatments. Parents might finally feel like they can be optimistic. And still others might realize all they have to offer the world through volunteer work or philanthropy. Whatever the odds, whatever the obstacles ... wishes find a way to make the world better.

gatorconnect.description: Women on Wall Street aims to introduce women to high finance roles such as Investment Banking, Global Capital Markets, Asset Management, Private Equity, and more. Currently, membership in top UF finance clubs and investment groups on campus is disproportionate, with women often comprising merely 20-35% of membership in an overall enrollment demographic of ~56% females. This disparity is partially due to decreased interest in comparison to males, as well as the high intimidation factor from the competitiveness within the field. High finance roles are often the earliest to recruit for junior summer (and therefore full-time) positions. Interview processes commence early-to-mid sophomore year and continue to move up. The past cycle began in early January. Potential candidates require intense information and preparation of industry dynamics, hierarchies, and technical and behavioral skills far in advance of these windows. We have noticed a disparity in how this information is communicated to many male students, who benefit from strong brotherhood pipelines, mentorship, and exclusivity primarily through fraternities or similar groups: communities inaccessible to female students. Women on Wall Street (WOW) was founded to address this information and mentorship gap. Our mission is to cultivate a supportive, performance-focused environment that equips members with the necessary knowledge, preparation, and network to excel on Wall Street and beyond. WWS is committed to developing a capable, technically proficient cohort of female finance students who meet the same recruiting standards as the majority of their male peers. The ultimate goal is to reshape how young women approach careers in finance by building a high-performing, merit-driven community that levels the playing field through skill, confidence, and rigorous training on the University of Florida campus and beyond.
gatorconnect.summary: Women on Wall Street’s empowers and prepares female underclassmen at the University of Florida for careers in high finance by providing early exposure, technical training, mentorship, and a supportive community.

gatorconnect.description: Words That Heal is a student organization dedicated to raising awareness about the importance of language access, effective communication, and patient understanding in healthcare. We recognize that communication is fundamental to quality patient care and that language barriers can affect a patient’s ability to describe symptoms, understand diagnoses and treatment plans, participate in medical decisions, and build trust with healthcare professionals. Our mission is to educate future healthcare professionals about these challenges while emphasizing the important role of qualified medical interpreters and accessible communication in medicine. Words That Heal seeks to prepare students to recognize language barriers, communicate more thoughtfully with diverse patient populations, and understand how effective communication can contribute to patient safety, trust, and quality of care. Throughout the year, members will have opportunities to participate in medical language workshops, educational presentations, guest speaker events, interactive healthcare communication activities, advocacy initiatives, and community outreach and service. Programming may introduce students to commonly encountered languages in healthcare while also exploring topics such as medical interpretation, health literacy, patient-provider communication, language access, and barriers faced by patients with limited English proficiency. Language workshops are intended to promote learning and awareness rather than replace the role of trained or qualified medical interpreters. Words That Heal also aims to connect students with physicians, medical interpreters, healthcare professionals, community organizations, and other student groups to provide opportunities to learn from individuals with firsthand experience addressing communication barriers in healthcare. Through these collaborations, members can better understand how language access functions in real clinical and community settings. The organization welcomes students of all majors, backgrounds, and language abilities. Members do not need to speak another language or be pursuing medicine to participate. By bringing together students interested in healthcare, languages, communication, service, and patient advocacy, Words That Heal hopes to foster an interdisciplinary community committed to improving the patient experience. Ultimately, Words That Heal strives to help create a future in which language does not prevent patients from understanding their healthcare or having their voices heard. By educating and engaging the next generation of healthcare professionals, we hope to reinforce a simple but essential principle: effective communication is an integral part of compassionate, patient-centered care.
gatorconnect.summary: Words That Heal educates future healthcare professionals about language access and communication in medicine through workshops, speakers, advocacy, and community outreach to help ensure every patient is heard and understood.

gatorconnect.description: Young Americans for Liberty is the University of Florida chapter of the largest pro-liberty student organization in America. We identify, educate, train, and mobilize students committed to individual liberty, limited constitutional government, free markets, free expression, and a peaceful foreign policy. What we do: weekly chapter meetings, guest lectures, film screenings, campus tabling, and structured debates that invite disagreement rather than avoid it. We also train members in practical civic skills - public speaking, argumentation, coalition-building, and event organizing. We are a viewpoint-driven organization, and membership is open to every enrolled UF student regardless of whether they agree with us. If you are libertarian, classical liberal, limited-government conservative, undecided, or simply want to argue with us in good faith, you are welcome. The chapter is affiliated with the national organization Young Americans for Liberty, Inc. We charge no dues.
gatorconnect.summary: A pro-liberty student organization advancing individual liberty, limited constitutional government, free markets, and free expression through debates, speakers, and open forums. All students welcome, whether or not you agree with us.

gatorconnect.description: We are the local chapter of the Young Democratic Socialists of America, the youth wing of the Democratic Socialists of America. The YDSA organizes youth and students of all backgrounds on the basis of building a better world not possible under capitalism, patriarchy, and white supremacy. We believe Democratic Socialism to be the cure to these societal ills and we endeavor to create a an equitable based on such values. In Gainesville, our chapter has been involved in campaigns for Amendment 4, Trans rights and Bodily autonomy, anti-austerity, and Palestine/BDS. Currently we are organizing to build a sanctuary campus, or a campus free from ICE and the imperialist institutions of our society. We seek to win our demands and fulfill our campaign by building a mass organization of youth in Gainesville and we invite all students interested in joining us as we carry out political education, mutual aid, campaign work, and more.
